title: Bacterial spot disease in outdoor tomatoes - Tanzania

Header: Bacterial spot disease in outdoor tomatoes - Tanzania

Prevention: Use non-infected clean seeds from healthy tomatoes, or from a and authorized dealer dealer, because this bacterial disease also lives in seeds.
Kill disease on <1 year old tomato seeds by soaking them in approx. 50°C water for 25 minutes, then cooling and drying.
Select nursery sites away from tomato and pepper fields, and change nursery sites every growing season.
Wet weather, rain splash and crowded planting favour the spread of the disease.
Use furrow irrigation instead of sprinkler irrigation to reduce disease spread.
Avoid working in fields under wet conditions.
Avoid mechanical damage to plant and fruits, because the bacteria enter the plant through wounds.
This bacterium does not live for very long in the soil.
Thus interrupt tomato growing for at least 2 seasons.

Keep volunteer tomato plants or other
Solanaceae out of fallow fields; because the disease can survive in them, as well as in their plant debris in the soil.
Monitoring: Bacterial spot attacks all growth stages of tomatoes.
Search for small water-soaked spots on leaves, stems, fruits.
Small round or irregular greasy dark green spots are first seen on the undersides of leaves.
As spots grow to 2-3 mm, they become purple-grey with a black centre.
Spots are sometimes surrounded by a yellow ring.
Search fruits for small pale green raised areas surrounded by a water- soaked border.
Old spots turn brownish and become raised and scabby, are sometimes surrounded by a whitish ring.
Spots of this disease do not go deeply into fruit, but allow other fungi and bacteria to rot the fruit.
If typical symptoms appear on leaves of about 5 to 10% of the plant population, action is suggested.
Direct Control: It is easier to prevent this disease than to control it.
Remove infected seedlings and young plants with roots and surrounding soil and burn or deeply bury everything.
Do not re-plant tomatoes in the same spot.
Restrictions: Prevention is the most powerful and often only measure (see first column).
Chemical products can only slightly suppress further spread of this disease.
However, there are currently no least toxic or slightly toxic products available.
